newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares end almost 3 pct higher, record close.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares end almost 3 pct higher, record close.

text.p: Dutch shares closed at a new record on Wednesday but the opening was even more spectacular since the index of 25 leading stocks broke the 1000-barrier for the first time in history when the market opened up at 0730 GMT.
Dealers said business was boosted by a buoyant close on Wall Street, a rising dollar and a firmer bond market.
"Business was also very much option driven today," said one dealer, adding volumes in the share market were not extreme.
The AEX share index closed almost three percent or 27.86 points higher at 988.48. The index jumped 45.64 points up to 1006.26 when trade started this morning.
The main index has almost doubled in just one year. On July 24, 1996 the AEX hit 508.81 points.

"Technically speaking there should be a correction coming up," said one dealer, adding he did not expect the index to drop much more than 100 points. "But, even if the index falls 150 points it does not wash away all the recent gains," he said.
The dealer added the correction could also be postponed till later since the dollar continued its uptrend, the bond market was strong and other surrounding share markets were also booming.
The AMX Midcap closed 41.16 points higher at 1508.82.

Among the stocks in the AMX index Semiconductor equipment maker ASM Lithography set a new record rising to 185.00 guilders in early trade. ASM Lithography announced a big rise in first half 1997 net profit to 147 million guilders.
The stock ended 16.40 guilders higher at 178.20.
Electronics firm Philips rose strongly ahead of Thursday's announcement on its second quarter results. Philips closed 9.40 guilders higher at 162.10.
Only very few stocks dipped and dealers blamed the drop of 2.60 guilders to 277.40 of publisher Wolters Kluwer on profit taking. It had risen over 20 guilders in a week.
"Some more stocks could be hit by profit taking on Thursday and Friday," said one dealer, adding financials, Unilever and Philips had been performing very well recently.
Bank-insurer ING closed 1.80 guilders higher at 104.00. ABN AMRO bank added 1.60 guilders to 49.90, after hitting a high of 52.50 guilders.
Insurer Aegon gained 6.00 guilders to 161.00. Fortis Amev ended 4.00 guilders up at 98.90.
